metadata.title: Phage Display Biopanning (M13 Ph.D. peptide library, surface panning by direct target coating)
metadata.purpose: Enrich M13 filamentous-phage clones displaying target-binding peptides from a randomized library by iterative rounds of affinity selection (biopanning): bind the library to an immobilized target, wash away non-binders, elute and amplify the bound phage, and repeat the selection 3 (up to 4) times until a consensus binding sequence emerges.
metadata.scope: Surface panning by direct adsorption of a purified target to polystyrene, using the NEB Ph.D. combinatorial peptide library (M13KE, peptide fused to pIII). Covers rounds 1-3 (optionally 4) with increasing wash stringency, amplification in E. coli ER2738, and titering. Not covered here: solution-phase panning with streptavidin/bead capture, phage ELISA and DNA sequencing of clones (post-panning characterization), or library cloning/construction.
metadata.estimatedTime: ~6 days (Day 1 coat; Day 2 round-1 bind/elute/amplify; Day 3 titer + recoat; Days 4-5 round 2; Day 6 round 3)
beforeYouBegin: Streak E. coli ER2738 onto an LB+Tet plate the day before and start a fresh overnight/early-log culture for infection and titering; the host must carry the F factor (grow on Tet).
Decide the elution strategy: specific competitive elution with a known ligand (0.1-1 mM) or free target (~100 ug/ml) vs general low-pH Glycine-HCl elution; this protocol defaults to Glycine-HCl.
Plan the iteration: input phage per round is held constant at ~1e11 virions; wash Tween-20 rises from 0.1% (round 1) to 0.5% (rounds 2-3) to raise stringency.
Prepare all buffers (Blocking Buffer, TBS, TBST, Glycine Elution Buffer, neutralization Tris, PEG/NaCl) and pre-warm LB/IPTG/Xgal titering plates.

materials.name: Ph.D. M13 phage display peptide library

materials.rawText: Blocking Buffer: 0.1 M NaHCO3 (pH 8.6), 5 mg/ml BSA, 0.02% NaN3 (optional).

materials.rawText: TBST (TBS + 0.1% [v/v] Tween-20). ... raising the Tween concentration in the wash steps to 0.5% (v/v)

materials.rawText: E. coli ER2738 host strain (F' ... zzf::Tn10(TetR) ...)

samples.name: Input phage pool (per round)
samples.description: Naive library in round 1 (~1e11 virions); in rounds 2+ this is the amplified eluate from the previous round, adjusted to the same input titer.

samples.name: Unbound (non-binding) phage
samples.description: Phage poured off after binding and removed during the wash steps; discarded.

samples.name: Eluted phage (unamplified eluate)
samples.description: Target-bound phage released by acid/competitive elution and neutralized; a small aliquot is titered.

samples.name: Amplified eluate
samples.description: Eluted phage propagated in ER2738 and PEG-purified (~1e13-1e14 pfu/mL); becomes the input for the next round.

samples.name: Enriched round-3 phage pool
samples.description: Final unamplified round-3 eluate; the selection output from which individual blue plaques are picked for sequencing/ELISA.

samples.name: Individual phage clones
samples.description: Blue plaques picked from round-3 titering plates for characterization (out of scope here).

containers.name: 60 x 15 mm polystyrene petri dish (or 96-well microtiter well)

tables.title: Per-round iteration matrix (repeat-until-enrichment loop; schema has no native loop construct)
rows: same input titer as round 1, from round-1 amplified eluate
same input titer as round 1, from round-2 amplified eluate
only if round 3 shows no consensus / negative ELISA
tables.note: Each round feeds the next: round N amplified eluate = round N+1 input. Input phage number is held constant (~1e11) across rounds; stringency is raised by increasing Tween from 0.1% to 0.5% after round 1. Loop exit condition: stop after round 3 (or 4) once a clear consensus binding sequence / positive phage ELISA is obtained.

tables.title: Elution options (choose one per interaction)
rows: 0.2 M Glycine-HCl pH 2.2, 1 mg/mL BSA, 1 mL (100 uL microtiter)
150 uL (15 uL microtiter) 1 M Tris-HCl pH 9.1, immediately
Known ligand 0.1-1 mM, or free target ~100 ug/mL, in TBS, 1 mL

tables.title: Titer / enrichment tracking (fill in during the run)
tables.note: Amplified culture supernatants typically titer 1e8-1e11; unamplified panning eluates 1e1-1e4 pfu per 10 uL; amplified eluate ~1e13-1e14 pfu/mL. A rising recovery (output/input) across rounds indicates successful enrichment.

steps.action: Prepare 10-100 ug/mL target in 0.1 M NaHCO3 (pH 8.6); add 1.5 mL (150 uL for microtiter wells) to the dish/well and swirl until the surface is completely wet.

parameters.rawText: 10-100 ug/ml of the target
Add 1.5 ml of this solution (150 ul if using microtiter wells)
0.1 M NaHCO3, pH 8.6

steps.expectedResult: Target-coating solution evenly covers the surface.
steps.criticalNotes: Solution may bead up on the hydrophobic polystyrene; swirl repeatedly. Do not add DTT if using the Ph.D.-C7C disulfide-constrained library.

sourceReferences.excerpt: Prepare a solution of 10-100 ug/ml of the target in 0.1 M NaHCO3, pH 8.6.

steps.action: Incubate overnight at 4 C with gentle agitation in a humidified container to adsorb the target.

parameters.rawText: incubate overnight at 4 C
overnight

steps.expectedResult: Target immobilized on the surface. Coated plates may be stored at 4 C in a humidified container.
steps.criticalNotes: Discard if mold appears on the damp paper towels.

steps.action: Inoculate 10 mL LB+Tet with ER2738 for titering; if amplifying the same day, also inoculate 20 mL LB in a 250 mL flask and grow to early-log (OD600 0.01-0.05).

parameters.rawText: Inoculate 10 ml of LB+Tet medium
20 ml of LB medium in a 250-ml Erlenmeyer flask
early-log phase (OD600 0.01-0.05)

steps.expectedResult: Host cultures growing; amplification culture must not exceed early-log.
steps.criticalNotes: Use a 250 mL Erlenmeyer flask, not a 50 mL conical tube, for the amplification culture (aeration).

steps.action: Pour off the coating solution, slap the plate face-down on a clean paper towel, fill completely with Blocking Buffer, and incubate at least 1 h at 4 C.

parameters.rawText: Incubate for at least 1 hour at 4 C
at 4 C

steps.expectedResult: Uncoated surface blocked against non-specific phage binding.

steps.action: Discard blocking buffer; wash the plate rapidly 6 times with TBST (0.1% Tween-20 in round 1), swirling to coat bottom and sides, pouring off, and slapping face-down on a fresh paper-towel section each time. Work quickly so the plate never dries.

parameters.rawText: Wash each plate rapidly 6 times with TBST
TBST (TBS + 0.1% [v/v] Tween-20)

steps.expectedResult: Excess/loosely bound material removed; surface ready for the library.
steps.criticalNotes: Do not add DTT with the Ph.D.-C7C library. In rounds 2-3 use 0.5% Tween-20 (see table t1).

steps.action: Dilute a 100-fold library representation (~1e11 virions; e.g. 2e11 phage for a 2e9-clone library) in 1 mL TBST (100 uL for microtiter), pipette onto the coated plate, and rock gently 10-60 min at room temperature.

parameters.rawText: the number of input phage should remain the same (1e11 virions)
with 1 ml of TBST (100 ul if using microtiter wells)
rock gently for 10-60 minutes at room temperature

steps.expectedResult: Target-binding phage captured on the surface.

sourceReferences.excerpt: Dilute a 100-fold representation of the library (e.g., 2 x 10^11 phage for a library with 2 x 10^9 clones) with 1 ml of TBST

steps.action: Discard non-binding phage by pouring off and slapping face-down on a clean paper towel, then wash the plate 10 times with TBST, using a clean paper-towel section each time.

parameters.rawText: Wash plates 10 times with TBST

steps.expectedResult: Weak/non-specific binders removed; only tight binders retained.
steps.criticalNotes: Increasing wash number/Tween in later rounds raises stringency and drives enrichment.

steps.action: Elute bound phage with 1 mL (100 uL microtiter) Glycine Elution Buffer (0.2 M Glycine-HCl pH 2.2, 1 mg/mL BSA), rocking gently 10-20 min at RT; alternatively elute specifically with 0.1-1 mM ligand or ~100 ug/mL free target in TBS (see table t2).

parameters.rawText: Elute bound phage with 1 ml (100 ul if using microtiter wells)
0.2 M Glycine-HCl (pH 2.2), 1 mg/ml BSA
rock gently for no more than 10-20 minutes

steps.expectedResult: Bound phage released into the eluate.
steps.safetyNotes: Glycine-HCl elution buffer is strongly acidic (pH 2.2).

steps.action: Pipette the eluate into a microcentrifuge tube and, if using Glycine Elution Buffer, immediately neutralize with 150 uL (15 uL microtiter) of 1 M Tris-HCl pH 9.1.

parameters.rawText: neutralize with 150 ul (15 ul for microtiter wells) of 1 M Tris-HCl, pH 9.1
1 M Tris-HCl, pH 9.1

steps.criticalNotes: Neutralized eluate may be stored at 4 C for up to ~1 week (pause point).

steps.action: Titer ~1 uL of the eluate on LB/IPTG/Xgal plates (count blue plaques), then amplify the rest by adding it to the 20 mL early-log ER2738 culture and shaking vigorously 4.5 h at 37 C.

parameters.rawText: Titer a small amount (~1 ul) of the eluate
incubating with vigorous shaking for 4.5 hours at 37 C
at 37 C

steps.expectedResult: Eluate titer recorded (unamplified eluates ~1e1-1e4 pfu per 10 uL); amplification culture propagating phage.
steps.criticalNotes: Optionally store neutralized eluate overnight at 4 C and amplify next day using a 1:100-diluted overnight ER2738 culture.

steps.action: Clarify the amplification culture by centrifuging 10 min at 12,000 g, 4 C; re-spin the supernatant; transfer the upper 80% and precipitate phage with 1/6 volume 20% PEG/2.5 M NaCl at 4 C for at least 2 h (preferably overnight).

parameters.rawText: spin for 10 minutes at 12,000 g at 4 C
spin for 10 minutes
add to it 1/6 volume of 20% PEG/2.5 M NaCl
precipitate at 4 C for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight

steps.expectedResult: Phage precipitated (visible white smear after spinning).

steps.action: Spin the PEG precipitate 15 min at 12,000 g, 4 C; resuspend the pellet in 1 mL TBS; microcentrifuge 5 min at 14,000 rpm, 4 C to pellet residual cells; transfer supernatant and reprecipitate with 1/6 volume PEG/NaCl on ice 15-60 min.

parameters.rawText: Spin the PEG precipitation at 12,000 g for 15 minutes at 4 C
Suspend the pellet in 1 ml of TBS
spin at maximum (14,000 rpm) for 5 minutes at 4 C
Incubate on ice for 15-60 minutes

steps.action: Microcentrifuge 10 min at 14,000 rpm, 4 C; discard supernatant, re-spin briefly, remove residual liquid; resuspend the pellet in 200 uL TBS and clarify 1 min. This supernatant is the amplified eluate. Titer it on LB/IPTG/Xgal (expect ~1e13-1e14 pfu/mL).

parameters.rawText: Microcentrifuge at 14,000 rpm for 10 minutes at 4 C
Suspend the pellet in 200 ul of TBS
phage titer, which should be on the order of 10^13-14 pfu/ml

steps.expectedResult: Amplified eluate (~1e13-1e14 pfu/mL) ready to seed the next round; storable up to 3 weeks at 4 C, or add equal volume glycerol for -20 C.
steps.criticalNotes: Use this titer to compute the input volume giving the same input as round 1 (step s6).

steps.action: ITERATE the selection. Round 2: recoat a plate (repeat s1-s2) and repeat the round using the round-1 amplified eluate as input at the same input titer, but raise TBST Tween-20 to 0.5% (repeat s4-s13). Round 3: recoat and repeat s4-s9 with 0.5% Tween using the round-2 amplified eluate; titer the round-3 eluate but do NOT amplify it. See table t1 for the full per-round matrix.

branches.condition: Clear consensus sequence obtained or phage ELISA positive after round 3
branches.action: Exit the loop; pick blue plaques for characterization (do not amplify the round-3 eluate for a further round).

branches.condition: No clear consensus / phage ELISA negative after round 3
branches.action: Amplify the round-3 eluate and carry out a 4th round of panning (repeat from the coating/blocking cycle), keeping 0.5% Tween.

parameters.rawText: After 3 rounds ... Do not amplify the third round eluate and carry out a fourth round of panning unless the characterization shows no clear consensus sequence or phage ELISA results are negative.
raising the Tween concentration in the wash steps to 0.5% (v/v)
at an input titer equivalent to what was used in the first round

steps.expectedResult: Progressive enrichment of target-binding clones; rising output/input recovery across rounds; an enriched round-3 (or round-4) phage pool.
steps.criticalNotes: The schema has no native loop/iteration construct: this single step encodes the repeat-until-enrichment cycle via a per-round table (t1), a back-edge branch (targetStepId s4), and a decisionPoint. Each round's amplified eluate is the next round's input (sp4 -> sp1). Round 3 is not amplified unless a 4th round is required.

sourceReferences.excerpt: Carry out a second round of panning: repeat Steps 4-18 ... raising the Tween concentration in the wash steps to 0.5% ... Carry out a third round of panning: repeat steps 4-10 ... It is not necessary to amplify the third round eluate.

steps.action: Titer the unamplified final-round eluate on LB/IPTG/Xgal and pick blue plaques for individual-clone characterization (DNA sequencing and phage ELISA); keep titering-plate incubation under 18 h at 37 C to avoid insert deletions.

parameters.rawText: incubated at 37 C for no longer than 18 hours, as deletions may occur if the plates are incubated longer

steps.expectedResult: Individual clones ready for sequencing/ELISA (characterization itself is out of scope of this protocol).
steps.criticalNotes: Pick plaques within 1-3 days of plating; set up clone overnights from a colony, not by diluting a titering culture.

controls.name: Streptavidin control panning (positive-control selection)
controls.description: Run a parallel selection against streptavidin; after 3 rounds the consensus should contain the His-Pro-Gln (HPQ) motif, confirming the library and panning workflow are functional.

controls.name: Titer both input and output each round
controls.description: Record input titer and unamplified-eluate output titer per round; a rising output/input recovery ratio is the readout that enrichment is occurring (table t3).

controls.name: Blue/white plaque screen
controls.description: Plate all titers on LB/IPTG/Xgal; recombinant M13KE plaques are blue, while contaminating wild-type/environmental phage give white plaques.

controls.name: No-target adsorption control
controls.description: Manufacturer notes a separate no-target panning is not productive; instead monitor enrichment and use a known positive target as the workflow control.

expectedOutputs: An enriched phage pool after 3 (optionally 4) rounds of panning, with rising output/input recovery across rounds.
A consensus target-binding peptide sequence among sequenced clones (the primary success criterion).
Amplified eluate stocks (~1e13-1e14 pfu/mL) for each round, and individual blue plaques for downstream sequencing/ELISA.

troubleshooting.solution: Amplify the round-3 eluate and perform a 4th round; consider switching to a solution-phase panning method.
Always plate on LB/IPTG/Xgal; severe white-plaque contamination can spoil subsequent rounds - use fresh cultures and clean technique.

troubleshooting.cause: Wash stringency too low; blocking insufficient
troubleshooting.solution: Increase wash number and raise Tween-20 to 0.5% in later rounds; ensure >=1 h blocking; keep plates from drying.

troubleshooting.problem: Amplified eluate titer too low to seed next round
troubleshooting.solution: Succeeding rounds can be run with as little as 1e9 pfu input phage; verify ER2738 was early-log at infection.

troubleshooting.problem: Loss of insert / deletions in clones
troubleshooting.solution: Keep titering-plate incubation under 18 h at 37 C and pick plaques within 1-3 days.

safety: Sodium azide (in Blocking Buffer) is toxic and forms explosive metal azides in plumbing - dispose per institutional rules.
DMF in the IPTG/Xgal stock is flammable and toxic - handle in a fume hood.
Glycine-HCl elution buffer is strongly acidic (pH 2.2); 1 M Tris pH 9.1 is basic - handle with care.
Work with E. coli and bacteriophage using standard microbiological (BSL-1) aseptic technique.
limitations: The canonical schema has no loop/iteration primitive, so the 3-5 identical selection rounds are represented as one full explicit round (steps s1-s13) plus a single iteration step (s14) that carries a per-round parameter table (t1), a back-edge branch, and a decisionPoint. Target identity, exact target concentration within 10-100 ug/mL, PEG/NaCl exact formulation, and library complexity are user/kit-specific and flagged needsReview. Downstream clone characterization (sequencing, phage ELISA) is out of scope. Numbers are for 60x15 mm petri dishes (microtiter volumes in parentheses).
